title: ～つもりだ — “I intend to ～”
summary: Verb dictionary form + つもりです says what you plan or intend to do. It shows a personal decision that you have already made in your mind. The negative is ない form + つもりです, or 〜つもりはありません.

patterns.form: 動詞辞書形＋つもりです
patterns.gloss: dictionary form + つもりです (行くつもりです)

patterns.form: 動詞ない形＋つもりです
patterns.gloss: ない-form + つもりです: intend not to (行かないつもりです)

body.p: Put the verb in the dictionary form and add つもりです: 行く → 行くつもりです, 寝る → 寝るつもりです. It is used for what you plan to do from now on.
つもり shows your own will or plan, not an outside schedule. Compare 来年日本へ行くつもりです (my plan) with 来年日本へ行きます (a firm statement or schedule). It is a softer way to say what you have in mind.
Two ways to deny: 行かないつもりです (I plan not to go) and 行くつもりはありません (I have no intention of going), which is stronger.

examples.ja: 来年（らいねん）日本（にほん）へ行（い）くつもりです。
examples.romaji: Rainen Nihon e iku tsumori desu.
examples.tr: I intend to go to Japan next year.

examples.ja: 今日（きょう）は早（はや）く寝（ね）るつもりです。
examples.romaji: Kyō wa hayaku neru tsumori desu.
examples.tr: I intend to go to bed early today.

examples.ja: 夏（なつ）休（やす）みに海（うみ）へ行（い）くつもりです。
examples.romaji: Natsuyasumi ni umi e iku tsumori desu.
examples.tr: I intend to go to the sea during summer break.

pitfalls: Use the dictionary form: 行くつもり, not 行きますつもり.
つもり is about your own intention. Don't use it to state another person's plan as a fact.
